content: Saga pattern: choreography = services publish/react to events with no central coordinator, fits simple flows with few participants; orchestration = a central coordinator (owning service or dedicated engine like Camunda/Temporal) commands each step and manages compensations, fits complex flows. For 2-3 service sagas (order/inventory/notification) via SQS, a lightweight 'orchestrator-in-the-owning-service' approach (order-service holds the saga state machine, sends commands, consumes reply/event queues) is common practice and avoids pulling in a dedicated orchestration engine.
